newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng roars to record, ends above 14,000.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng roars to record, ends above 14,000.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index roared to a new all-time high on Wednesday, bursting through 14,000 points and closing above that level for the first time ever as HSBC Holdings led a powerful advance.
The blue-chip index jumped 247.12 points, or 1.78 percent, to close at an all-time high of 14,153.58.
Turnover was the third heaviest in history at HK$17.70 billion, up from HK$15.23 billion on Tuesday.
"Momentum is a lot stronger than people thought," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
"I think the market can still move up a bit in the next few days. There is a lot of liquidity," he added.
Analysts said a sudden surge in prices during late-morning had taken them by surprise.

Standard & Poor's upgrade of Hong Kong's foreign and local currency credit ratings on Wednesday had bolstered sentiment, they said. The international credit agency also fuelled a surge of HK$6.00 in HSBC Holdings shares to a close of HK$223.00 by raising its long-term ratings on the bank.
"This is a good endorsement that it is business as usual in Hong Kong," said South China Brokerage director Howard Gorges.
